# How to Use Claude Code to Sort a Messy Downloads Folder on Your Computer

> **In short:** Claude Code is a tool from Anthropic that works inside a text window on your computer. You can point it at your Downloads folder, ask for a sorting plan, and approve the moves only after reading it. It needs a Claude account with access to Claude Code, and it can only see the folder you open it in.

By the end of this guide, you'll have Claude Code look at a cluttered folder, suggest how to organize it, and move files only after you've read and approved the plan. This is for anyone whose Downloads folder has turned into a pile of PDFs, screenshots and mystery files. You don't need to be a programmer, but you will type a few short commands into a window that may look unfamiliar. We'll go slowly.

## Before you start

- **A computer, not a phone.** Claude Code runs in a terminal, a text-based window. On a Mac it's called Terminal, and on Windows you'll use PowerShell or Command Prompt.
- **A Claude account with access to Claude Code.** Check Anthropic's official Claude Code page for which plans include it. It may require a paid plan or API billing, so look at the current details there before you start.
- **About 30–45 minutes**, including setup. Sorting itself usually takes a few minutes.

## Step 1 — Make a practice copy first

Before Claude Code touches anything real, create a safe test folder. On your Desktop, make a new folder called **Practice Downloads**. Then copy 10 to 20 files from your real Downloads folder into it. Copying leaves the originals where they are, so nothing is lost.

Pick a mix: a PDF, a few images, a zip file, anything you'd expect to find in Downloads. If you're unsure what to choose, a random assortment works fine. Your practice folder is where you'll learn how Claude Code behaves, and you'll only move on to your real folder once you trust the process.

💬 Example: after copying, you can ask yourself, "Do I have a folder with about 15 files I don't mind experimenting on?"

You'll know it worked when your Practice Downloads folder contains copies of real files and your original Downloads folder still looks the same.

## Step 2 — Install Claude Code and sign in

Go to Anthropic's official Claude Code page and follow its installation instructions for your operating system. Copy commands only from that official page, not from random websites. Once it's installed, the tool will ask you to sign in with your Claude account, usually by opening a browser window. Sign in there, then return to the terminal.

If the install steps look confusing, that's normal. Installation changes over time, so trust the official page over anything you read elsewhere, including this guide. If an install step fails, copy the exact error message and check the official troubleshooting section.

You'll know it worked when you can type the command `claude` in a terminal window and see Claude Code start up instead of an error saying the command isn't found.

## Step 3 — Open the terminal inside your practice folder

Open your terminal app. On a Mac, search for **Terminal** in Spotlight. On Windows, search for **PowerShell** in the Start menu. Then move the terminal into your practice folder. A common way is to type `cd` followed by a space, then drag the **Practice Downloads** folder from your Desktop into the window. The path should appear after the `cd`. Press Enter.

If dragging doesn't work on your system, type the folder's location by hand. For example, on a Mac it might look like `cd ~/Desktop/Practice\ Downloads`. Your exact path may differ, so check where the folder actually lives.

💬 Example: type `cd` and a space, then drag in the folder, then press Enter.

You'll know it worked when the line at the bottom of the terminal ends with the name of your practice folder.

## Step 4 — Start Claude Code and ask for a plan only

Type `claude` and press Enter. A welcome screen should appear, along with a text box where you can type. Now ask for a plan without any moves. This step is the most important one, because it keeps you in control.

Type a request like the example below. Claude Code will read the files in the folder it can see and describe what it would do. It shouldn't change anything yet. If it starts moving files without showing you a plan, press the Escape key to stop it, then type a clearer request.

💬 Example: "Look at the files in this folder and propose a plan to sort them into subfolders by type, such as Documents, Pictures and Archives. Do not move or rename anything yet. Show me the plan as a numbered list."

You'll know it worked when Claude Code replies with a list of proposed folders and which files would go into each one, and none of your files have moved yet.

## Step 5 — Read the plan and approve part of it

Read the list slowly. Ask yourself: Does each group make sense to me? Is anything going into a folder I wouldn't expect? If something looks wrong, reply and ask for changes, such as, "Move the screenshots into a folder called [screenshot folder name] instead." Keep going until the plan matches how you'd like things organized.

When you're happy with part of it, approve only that part. For example, you might say, "Yes, do only the first two groups for now." Claude Code usually asks for your permission before it edits or moves files, and it may show you each action and wait for a yes. Read each request before you approve it. If it asks for permission to run a command you don't understand, it's fine to say no and ask it to explain.

💬 Example: "Looks good. Go ahead with the Documents and Pictures groups only, and leave everything else where it is."

You'll know it worked when the files in those groups appear in their new subfolders and everything else stays put.

## Step 6 — Check the results and then decide about your real folder

Open your Practice Downloads folder in Finder (Mac) or File Explorer (Windows) and look inside. Check that each file is where you expected and that nothing went missing. If you spot a problem, ask Claude Code to undo it, or move the file back yourself. Keep the practice folder until you're confident.

Only after the practice run feels comfortable should you repeat the process on your real Downloads folder. Make a backup first if you have any important files there, such as an external drive or cloud copy. Then open the terminal inside your real Downloads folder and follow Steps 3 through 5 again.

💬 Example: "Summarize what you moved, and list any files you skipped and why."

You'll know it worked when the summary matches what you see in the folder, and you can find every file you care about.

## Common mistakes

- **Approving the whole plan without reading it.** Read each group first. If a folder name or file group is unclear, ask Claude Code to explain it before you say yes.
- **Starting with your real Downloads folder.** Practice on a copy first. Once you've seen how it behaves, you can move on with much less worry.
- **Expecting it to know what matters to you.** Claude Code can guess from file names and types, but it can't know that a file is your passport scan or a draft you're still editing. Keep important files backed up, and keep an eye on anything personal.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** Once you trust the process, a cluttered Downloads folder can become a tidy set of folders in an afternoon, and the approve-first habit keeps you in charge.
- **For your business or work:** The same plan-then-approve method works for project folders, invoice archives and shared drives, as long as you check the plan and keep backups before any bulk moves.
- **If you're just getting started:** Begin with the practice folder and only ask for a plan. Reading a proposal costs nothing, and it shows you how Claude Code thinks before it does any real work.

## Try it now

Open your Downloads folder, count roughly how many files are sitting in the top level, and note the three most common file types. Then copy five of them into a new practice folder on your Desktop. That gives you a safe, small test to start with the next time you sit down with Claude Code.
